title: RNNs & LSTMs: Memory, BPTT and Exploding Gradients
summary: How recurrent networks carry a hidden state through a sequence, how backpropagation through time computes their gradients, why those gradients vanish or explode, and how LSTM gates and global-norm clipping keep training stable.
takeaways: An RNN reuses the same weights at every step, and each step's hidden state feeds the next.
BPTT walks backwards in time. Each hidden state's gradient is the local loss gradient plus what flows back from the future.
Repeated multiplication by W_h makes gradients vanish or explode. Clip by the global norm, which preserves direction.
LSTM gates (i, f, o) are sigmoids, and the candidate g is a tanh. An additive cell update lets gradients survive long spans.

flow.title: Training a recurrent network on one sequence

steps.label: Unroll
steps.detail: For t = 0…T−1, compute h_t (and c_t) from x_t and the previous state.

steps.label: Loss
steps.detail: Read predictions from some or all hidden states and sum the losses.

steps.label: BPTT
steps.detail: Walk t = T−1…0, adding dh from the loss to dh flowing back from t+1. Accumulate weight gradients.

steps.label: Clip
steps.detail: If the global gradient norm exceeds max_norm, scale every gradient by max_norm / norm.

steps.label: Update
steps.detail: Apply the optimizer step with the clipped gradients.

terms.definition: The vector h_t an RNN carries between time steps, summarizing everything seen so far.
Backpropagation through time: ordinary backprop applied to the unrolled recurrent network.
Gradients that grow exponentially with sequence length because of repeated multiplication by the recurrent weights.
Rescaling all gradients so their combined (global) L2 norm is at most a threshold.
The LSTM's additive memory c_t, written by the input gate and erased by the forget gate.
A sigmoid-valued vector in (0, 1) that multiplies another signal element-wise to control how much passes.
